   73|     """Custom QLIKE objective for LightGBM.
   74| 
   75|     Log-space QLIKE: L = exp(y_true - y_pred) - (y_true - y_pred) - 1
   76|     gradient (dL/dy_pred) = 1 - exp(y_true - y_pred)
   77|     hessian  (d²L/dy_pred²) = exp(y_true - y_pred)

   82|         Current predictions (log-RV space).

   92|     # Symmetric clip: pure overflow protection. exp(709) overflows float64.

   94|     # QLIKE's natural exponential already penalizes under-prediction harder.
   95|     diff = np.clip(y_true - y_pred, -10.0, 10.0)
   96|     exp_diff = np.exp(diff)
   97|     grad = 1.0 - exp_diff

   99|     return grad, hess

--- README.md ---
    1| # ml-vol-estimator
    2| 
    3| ML realized volatility forecasting — signal discovery. Progressively enriches HAR-family baselines with microstructure, options-implied, and cross-asset features via gradient boosting to produce statistically significant QLIKE improvements that translate into a tradeable IV-RV gap signal.
    4| 
    5| **Timeline:** ~20-week internship, May–Sep 2026.
    6| 
    7| ---
    8| 
    9| ## Quick Start
   10| 
   11| 1. Open `ml-vol-estimator.code-workspace` in VS Code.
   12| 2. Boot protocol loads automatically: `memory/person/user.md` + `memory/INDEX.md`.
   13| 3. Use `/bootup` to start a session — it reads the research journal and orients you.
   14| 4. Drive work with slash commands: `/research`, `/feature`, `/experiment`, `/backtest`.
   15| 
   16| See [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for the full project spec, and [workspace/docs/user-manual.md](workspace/docs/user-manual.md) for all commands.
   17| 
   18| ---
   19| 
   20| ## CLI
   21| 
   22| The `vol` wrapper handles uv, PATH, and working directory internally.
   23| 
   24| ### Wrapper Commands
   25| 
   26| ```
   27| vol test [args]               # pytest (extra args forwarded: -k, -v, --tb=short)
   28| vol testlf [args]             # re-run last-failed tests only
   29| vol run --config <yaml>       # primary entry point (see below)
   30| vol status                    # show data ingestion manifest
   31| vol lint                      # ruff check (read-only)
   32| vol fmt                       # ruff auto-format
   33| vol typecheck                 # mypy
   34| vol sync                      # install/update deps
   35| vol shell                     # REPL with volforecast importable
   36| vol notebook                  # jupyter
   37| vol help                      # usage
   38| ```
   39| 
   40| ### Primary Command: `vol run --config <yaml>`
   41| 
   42| Every `vol run --config` invocation uses the tournament code path — even single-model configs produce ranked tables and an interactive Plotly HTML dashboard. The only special case is `mode: ingest` (data ingestion only).
   43| 
   44| Optional overrides: `--symbols SPY,AAPL` (override YAML universe), `--skip-ingest` (skip data fetch), `--workers 8` (thread count).
   45| 
   46| ### Examples
   47| 
   48| ```bash
   49| # Single-model experiment (ingest + train + evaluate + dashboard)
   50| vol run --config workspace/configs/baseline_har.yaml
   51| 
   52| # Tournament: 13 models compared with statistical tests
   53| vol run --config workspace/configs/tournament_full_spy.yaml
   54| 
   55| # Skip ingestion (data already cached), subset of symbols
   56| vol run --config workspace/configs/tournament_har_dev.yaml --skip-ingest --symbols SPY,AAPL
   57| 
   58| # Ingest only
   59| vol run --config workspace/configs/ingest_full_universe.yaml --workers 8
   60|
